column1: > The distribution and network dimensions. Each row rebuilds the whole
> lab as that distribution with that container network and runs its
> suite: the named placement rows from scenarios.tsv, the named outage
> rows from outages.tsv, and then mechanism.sh asserts who balances
> the API path on the live remotes. "full" in a column means every row
> in that file. A row's key for ONLY_DISTRO and its logs is
> "<distro>-<cni>"; a bare distro name matches all of that
> distribution's rows.
> The cni column names an installer under cni.d/, or "default" for the
> network the distribution itself ships (k0s: kuberouter, k3s:
> embedded flannel, RKE2: canal; kubeadm ships none, so it has no
> default row). Native-routing networks (calico, kube-router) put pod
> addresses on the tunnel, so the mesh's accept lists carry each
> node's blocks; encapsulating networks (flannel vxlan, cilium tunnel,
> canal) address the tunnel's packets to nodes, and the controller's
> cni package models the difference from each network's own resources.
> The suite is deliberately not the full cross product. What varies by
> distribution is how the site is built, how a remote joins, and who
> balances the API path; what varies by network is who owns which
> prefix and whether the tunnel carries pod or node addresses. The
> all-nodes-two-clouds row (every pair, 112 checks) proves each combo's
> mesh whole; the outage rows re-prove recovery only where the
> distribution's mechanics differ, which is why the calico rows carry
> them and the other networks lean on the placement rows first.
> rke2 runs cp-dies' outage as reboots only, by recorded decision, not
> oversight: a sustained partition of an RKE2 server node wedges that
> node's etcd beyond the distribution's own recovery. rke2-server
> fatals on "leaderelection lost" (by design, expecting a clean
> restart), its containerd dies with it while the pod shims survive,
> and the orphaned etcd, its log consumer gone, keeps heartbeating
> raft while its serving paths block on a full stderr pipe; every
> restart then dies reading the datastore, forever, even after the
> partition heals. Measured here, recovered only by killing the
> orphaned etcd by hand (~3 minutes to Ready afterwards); known
> upstream (rancher/rke2 issues 4510, 4479, 7155). k3s embeds etcd in
> process, restarts it with itself, and passes the same row; power
> loss orphans nothing, so the reboot rows stand for rke2.
